The lower decomposes into a two-frequency extremum plus manifestly positive second-frequency terms; cubic derivative and interval root counts locate the unique minimum. The upper optimizes first and second magnitudes by an exact nonnegative square/cubic deficit; a second cubic derivative establishes a unique interior maximum. Both phase equalities, boundaries and quantifiers are checked. The packaged checker verifies symbolic identities and cubic counts using actual package source; finite random checks are only diagnostics.

value.rationale: The complete real six-dimensional norm range is natural for the first three nonconstant Fourier harmonics, the smallest case featuring two simultaneous fourth-order resonances. The minimum remains a two-tone optimizer despite allowing another harmonic, whereas the maximum uses all three with the first two equal. Distinct algebraic cubic extrema, a full equality classification and exact positive deficit identities give structural information not obtained from generic Nikolskii bounds or the known two-tone endpoint.
